AUTHOR: Varini
TITLE: SharkTrack: An accurate, generalisable software for streamlining shark and ray underwater video analysis
REGION: Training: BRUVS snippets from 25 locations worldwide (incl. Global FinPrint); test: Red Sea, Anguilla (Caribbean), North Malé Atoll (Maldives)
SPECIES: Single 'elasmobranch' class (sharks Selachii + rays Batoidea); species assigned manually by analysts (15/5/7 species in Red Sea/Anguilla/Maldives tests, e.g. nurse shark, grey reef shark)
DATA: Own/partner compiled BRUVS dataset: 77 video snippets (~2 h) from 25 locations, 1 fps frames, plus 587 Batoidea instances from Open Images (social media); 7049 annotated images. Test: 207 h of partner BRUVS footage (Red Sea, Anguilla, Maldives) with manual ssMaxN
V_EV: Sec. 3.1-3.2: 'Visibility was more than 5 m in most videos' (Red Sea); Caribbean 'In this turbid water, SharkTrack confused many of the algae'; per-location MaxN Accuracy in Table 1
D2: Train/val random 85:15 split on locations (not images); separate test set of 207 h BRUVS from 3 locations not in training
D_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'using a random 85:15 split on locations rather than images'; test 'BRUVS footage from three locations not represented in the training data'
R_EV: Sec. 3: 'We tested SharkTrack on three case studies of elasmobranch videos collected from novel locations not represented in the training data'
C_EV: Sec. 4: 'the average false positive rate was 86% (estimated by manually verifying 100 randomly sampled detections per location'; Sec. 2.2: 'confidence threshold of 0.2'
E_EV: Sec. 3: 'We compared the ground truth ssMaxN, computed manually, with the ssMaxN computed by analysts using the SharkTrack semi-automatic process'; 'average of 89% MaxN Accuracy'
ARCH: YOLOv8-nano single-class detector (640 px, conf 0.2, 500 epochs) + tuned BotSORT tracker with post-processing; human-in-the-loop species assignment propagated per track to compute ssMaxN
METR: Validation mAP50 0.85 (precision/recall/F1 in Supp. S2); test MaxN Accuracy 81.8% (Red Sea), 87.8% (Anguilla), 97.8% (Maldives), mean 89%; FP rate 86% (95% Caribbean) from manual check; inference and manual post-processing time (2 min per video-hour, 95% reduction)
NOTE: Elasmobranchs treated as fish (cartilaginous fishes) -> INCL Y; training includes some Open Images social-media ray photos, but headline evaluation is on in-situ BRUVS field footage. TAXA coded 과/속 수준 as closest value for a single higher-taxon class (subclass Elasmobranchii); verifier may prefer 어류 전체. D1 coded 지역: validation split by location and headline test on 3 regions absent from training; caveat: training contains 120 images from one Maldives video from a different BRUVS project/location (authors discuss this -> D4 Y). R2 복수 = new site/region plus different species composition (only 1/10 Maldives species shared) and water conditions (turbid Caribbean). R3 = N because in-domain metric (val mAP50) differs from external metric (MaxN Accuracy); no same-metric comparison. V1: 'visibility >5 m' is an eye estimate, coded 정성 서술만 (lower-information choice); V6 P because per-location results are linked to visibility described qualitatively. C5: FP rate measured by manual verification of 100 random detections per test location (field footage) -> 검증 표본 오탐률, C_ALL Y. Human analysts delete false positives in the pipeline; final ssMaxN is semi-automatic. Ground truth ssMaxN is human reading of the same footage, and the paper reports experts were wrong in 7% of instances. Metadata file new_meta.json had no S083 entry; bibliographic fields taken from the task brief. Pretraining weights not stated.
